1: # Rider Payout Dispute Desk
2: 
3: - ProcureYard take-home, ML/AI Engineer Intern.
4: - Due **24 hours after you receive the assignment email**. A 30-minute call follows.
5: - AI tools allowed. Python or Node.js, any agent framework or none, any LLM provider (the free tiers of Groq and Gemini are enough).
6: 
7: QuickDrop is a fictional delivery company with about 5,000 riders. Its ops team handed us the material below, as it came.
8: 
9: **Email from the Head of Ops**
10: 
11: > Subject: Fwd: rider payout complaints, please fix
12: >
13: > Every morning my three executives find hundreds of WhatsApp messages from riders saying their payout is wrong: "bhai kal ka payout 120 kam aaya", "order T88213 ka surge nahi mila". They check the trips sheet, work out what the rider should have got, compare it with what we paid, and reply. Two days per reply. Riders are angry, some have quit.
14: >
15: > I want an assistant that handles this the way my executives do: it talks to the rider, asks what it needs, checks the trips and payouts, and sorts it out. Riders reply in several messages, change their story, or complain about two things at once. If the rider is right, they get their money and a reply. If they're wrong, a proper explanation, not silence. Anything unclear or shady comes to my team, and my team needs to see what happened and why. I also need to trust it before it moves money.
16: >
17: > Meera
18: 
19: **Note from Finance**
20: 
21: > Auto-pay is fine for small amounts: up to ₹200 per dispute, once per rider per day. Bigger or repeat ones need someone from ops to approve. Never pay more than the rider is owed, we lost money on this last quarter. We reconcile against PaySwift, not against your database.
22: 
23: **Chat from the engineer who set up the messaging vendor**
24: 
25: > the vendor POSTs each rider message to us, one at a time, as the rider types them. if they don't get a 2
<truncated 108 bytes>
s sent from. whatever we return as reply goes back to the rider.
26: >
27: > PaySwift sandbox behaves like production.
28: 
29: **Interface**
30: 
31: ```
32: POST /messages
33: { "message_id": "wamid.KAZ5TCF7RARUVH", "rider_id": "R003",
34:   "text": "Bhai order T926334 ka surge nahi mila, 20 tarikh wala",
35:   "received_at": "2026-09-22T09:05:00+05:30" }
36: 
37: → { "reply": "text that goes back to the rider" }
38: 
39: GET /trace/{rider_id}   everything your agent did for this rider, in order
40: GET /ops/pending        what is waiting for ops: approvals and escalations
41: ```
42: 
43: **What to build**
44: 
45: - An agent that handles rider conversations end to end. You choose its tools, its memory and what the model is allowed to decide.
46: - Evals for your agent: one command that takes the service URL, runs your test conversations and prints a report. They may use only the interface above and PaySwift, because we will also run them against other implementations.
47: - A simple page where ops can see conversations and what the agent did, and approve or reject what's waiting.
48: - `docker compose up` runs everything: your service, Postgres and the PaySwift sandbox. GitHub Actions run on every push.
49: 
50: **In the repo** (https://github.com/Procureyard/qd-assignment): `docs/policy.md` (ops wiki), `data/` (exports from our systems, plus sample conversations with the end result we'd expect), `payswift/` (provider docs and sandbox). Everything else is yours to decide.
51: 
52: **Submit**
53: 
54: - Clone the repo (don't fork it), build in a new private repo of your own, add `Sarthak-pyard` as a collaborator, and reply to this email with the link before the deadline.
55: - README, one page maximum: how to run it, your agent's design (its tools, what the model decides and what your code decides), assumptions you made, your eval results, what you skipped.
56: - The raw exports of your AI sessions in `ai-logs/`, not summaries or screenshots. `SUBMISSION.md` has the logistics.

1: # Submission logistics
2: 
3: - `docker compose up` starts your whole system: your service, Postgres and the `payswift` service already defined in `docker-compose.yml`. Keep the `payswift` service as it is.
4: - Your service listens on port **8000** and answers `GET /health` with 200 when it is ready.
5: - Your service reads the PaySwift URL from the environment variable `PAYSWIFT_BASE_URL`.
6: - `POST /messages` returns `{"reply": "..."}`. You may add fields; we only rely on `reply`.
7: - `GET /trace/{rider_id}` returns a JSON list of steps in order. Each step has at least:
8:   `at` (ISO time), `type` (`message_in`, `tool_call`, `decision`, `reply`, or `error`), `name`, `input`, `output`.
9: - `GET /ops/pending` returns a JSON list of items waiting for ops. Each item has at least:
10:   `id`, `rider_id`, `type` (`approval` or `escalation`), `amount` (rupees, for approvals), `reason`, `created_at`.
11: - Your eval command is one line in your README and takes the service URL as its argument, for example `python evals/run.py http://localhost:8000`.
12: - List every environment variable your service needs in `.env.example`. Don't commit `.env` or any key.
13: - `ai-logs/` holds the raw exports of the AI sessions you used, one file per session. Where to find them:
14:   Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` · Codex CLI: `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-*.jsonl` or `codex export` ·
15:   Cursor: chat menu (…) → Export Chat · GitHub Copilot in VS Code: Command Palette → "Chat: Export Chat…" ·
16:   Gemini CLI: `/export jsonl --output <file>` · Antigravity: the chat export, or the `antigravity-history` tool · ChatGPT: Settings → Data controls → Export.
17:   If your tool has no export, include whatever it does provide and say what it is.
18: - We use whatever is on `main` of the repo you link when the deadline passes.
19: 
20: ## Output shapes
21: 
22: Only the shape is fixed. Step names, what goes in `input` and `output`, and how many steps there are depend entirely on how you design your agent.
23: 
24: `GET /trace/{rider_id}`
25: 
26: ```json
27: [
28:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "message_in", "name": "<name>", "input": {"message_id": "...", "text": "...", "received_at": "..."}, "output": null},
29:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "tool_call",  "name": "<your tool>", "input": {"<argument>": "..."}, "output": {"<result>": "..."}},
30:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "decision",   "name": "<what was decided>", "input": {"...": "..."}, "output": {"...": "..."}},
31:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "reply",      "name": "<name>", "input": null, "output": "<text sent to the rider>"}
32: ]
33: ```
34: 
35: `GET /ops/pending`
36: 
37: ```json
38: [
39:   {"id": "<id>", "rider_id": "<rider>", "type": "approval", "amount": 120, "reason": "<why it needs a human>", "created_at": "<ISO time>"},
40:   {"id": "<id>", "rider_id": "<rider>", "type": "escalation", "amount": null, "reason": "<why it needs a human>", "created_at": "<ISO time>"}
41: ]
42: ```

1: # Payout policy (pasted from the ops wiki)
2: 
3: - Every completed trip pays ₹25 base + ₹6 for each km after the first 2 km. If the trip had a surge multiplier, it applies to the whole trip fare (base + distance). Round each trip to the nearest rupee, 0.5 rounds up.
4: - Daily incentive of ₹150 for 12 or more trips in a day.
5: - ₹10 penalty for every trip the rider cancels. Customer cancellations earn nothing.
6: - "Day" means the calendar day in IST.
7: - We only look at disputes for the last 7 days.

1: `riders.csv`: rider_id, name, city, joined_on
2: 
3: `trips.csv`: trip_id, rider_id, started_at, status, distance_km, surge_multiplier. Status is `completed`, `cancelled_by_customer` or `cancelled_by_rider`. Exported from the trips system, 12 to 21 Sep 2026.
4: 
5: `payout_lines.csv`: line_id, payout_date, rider_id, line_type, trip_id, amount. What riders were actually paid. Line type is `trip`, `daily_incentive` or `cancellation_penalty`; penalties are negative.
6: 
7: `conversations.json`: sample conversations, from one message to several. Rider turns are what the vendor sends; agent turns, where shown, are an example of a good reply, not required wording. `expected` is how the conversation should end.
8: 
9: `expected` means:
10: - `payout`: rupees that should reach the rider in PaySwift because of this message or conversation (0 if none)
11: - `approval`: rupees that should be waiting for ops approval, or null
12: - `escalation`: `required`, `optional` or `no`
13: - `reply_mentions` (conversations only): facts the rider should be told
14: - `one_of` (conversations only): any one of the listed end states is acceptable
15: 
16: Run each conversation against a fresh system.

1: # PaySwift Payouts API (sandbox)
2: 
3: Runs with `docker compose up payswift` on port 8081. The ledger is in memory and is cleared on restart.

5: ```

11: ```

15: ```
16: GET /v1/payouts?rider_id=R017     list payouts (rider_id optional)
17: GET /health
18: ```
19: 
20: Rate limits apply.

---

### 1. Business Context & Problem Statement
- **Company**: QuickDrop (fictional on-demand delivery startup with ~5,000 riders).
- **Pain Point**: Ops executives spend days manually resolving WhatsApp complaints from riders about missing fares, missing surge pay, incentives, or wrongful cancellation penalties.
- **Goal**: Build an autonomous **Rider Payout Dispute Desk** agent that:
  - Chats with riders (typically in Hinglish / casual phrasing) to collect missing details.
  - Investigates trip records and past payouts against the official policy.
  - Automatically issues valid payouts via the **PaySwift** sandbox API within finance constraints.
  - Escalates suspicious, ambiguous, or large disputes to Ops via an approval queue.
  - Provides clear, transparent explanations to riders.

---

### 2. Payout Policy Rules ([`docs/policy.md`](file:///C:/Users/BIT/Desktop/Projects/Intern_assignment/Introduction/qd-assignment/docs/policy.md))
- **Base Fare**: ₹25 base + ₹6 per km for every km beyond the first 2 km.
- **Surge**: Applied as a multiplier to the *entire trip fare* (base + distance fare). Rounded to the nearest rupee (0.5 rounds up).
- **Daily Incentive**: ₹150 if a rider completes **12 or more** trips in a single calendar day (IST).
- **Cancellation Penalty**: ₹10 penalty deducted for every trip cancelled by the *rider*. Customer cancellations earn ₹0 (no penalty).
- **Dispute Window**: Only disputes from the **last 7 days** are eligible.

---

### 3. Financial & Operational Guardrails ([`BRIEF.md`](file:///C:/Users/BIT/Desktop/Projects/Intern_assignment/Introduction/qd-assignment/BRIEF.md))
- **Auto-pay Limits**: Max **₹200** per dispute, and at most **once per rider per day**.
- **Ops Approvals**: Any dispute > ₹200 or repeat disputes for the same rider on the s

- [`payout_lines.csv`](file:///C:/Users/BIT/Desktop/Projects/Intern_assignment/Introduction/qd-assignment/data/payout_lines.csv): 3,222 payout records actually disbursed.

### 6. Deliverables to Build
1. **Agent Engine & Service**: Core FastAPI/Express app handling conversation memory, tool execution (database queries, policy calculation, PaySwift calls), and response generation.
2. **Ops Dashboard**: Simple UI page for ops executives to view traces and approve/reject pending escalations.

6. **One-page README**: Architecture, decisions (model vs. deterministic code), evals, and assumptions.

- Cancelled by customer: 0 rupees.
- Daily incentive: 150 rupees for 12 or more completed trips in a single IST calendar day.
- 7-day dispute window: Disputed date must be within 7 calendar days before the message received_at date in IST.

import zoneinfo

IST = zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata")


def to_ist_datetime(dt_str_or_obj) -> datetime:
    """Converts an ISO string or datetime object to an aware IST datetime."""
    if isinstance(dt_str_or_obj, str):
        # Handle ISO strings with Z or offset
        clean_str = dt_str_or_obj.replace("Z", "+00:00")
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(clean_str)
    else:
        dt = dt_str_or_obj
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=IST)

    assert calculate_trip_fare(distance_km=2.0, surge_multiplier=1.0, status="completed") == 25

    # Run seeding from data/ directory

    seed_data_if_empty(base_data_dir=str(repo_data_dir))
    
    session = get_db_session()
    try:
        rider_count = session.query(Rider).count()
        trip_count = session.query(Trip).count()
        payout_count = session.query(PayoutLine).count()
        
        # Verify counts match CSV line counts
        assert rider_count == 40
        assert trip_count == 3314
        assert payout_count == 3222

        # Verify idempotency: calling seed_data_if_empty again shouldn't duplicate
        seed_data_if_empty(base_data_dir=str(repo_data_dir))
        assert session.query(Rider).count() == 40

        # Verify conversation messages unique message_id constraint
        msg1 = ConversationMessage(
            message_id="wamid.TEST1",
            rider_id="R001",
            text="hello",
            received_at=session.query(Trip).first().started_at

        session.add(msg1)
        session.commit()

        # Adding same message_id should fail
        msg2 = ConversationMessage(
            message_id="wamid.TEST1",
            rider_id="R001",
            text="hello again",
            received_at=session.query(Trip).first().started_at
        )
        session.add(msg2)
        with pytest.raises(Exception):

""""
FastAPI application for QuickDrop Rider Dispute Desk.
Implements:
- GET /health
- POST /messages (with wamid idempotency)
- GET /trace/{rider_id}
- GET /ops/pending
- Ops actions: POST /ops/{action}/{id}
- Ops HTML Dashboard on GET /ops
"""

import json
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Optional, List, Dict, Any
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.db import (
    init_db, seed_data_if_empty, get_db,
    ConversationMessage, Trace, OpsPending
)
from app.agent import DisputeAgent
from app.payswift_client import PaySwiftClient


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Initialize DB and seed CSV datasets if empty
    init_db()
    seed_data_if_empty()
    yield


app = FastAPI(title="QuickDrop Rider Dispute Desk", lifespan=lifespan)
agent = DisputeAgent()


# ----------------- Request / Response Models -----------------

class MessageRequest(BaseModel):
    message_id: str
    rider_id: str
    text: str
    received_at: str


class MessageResponse(BaseModel):
    reply: str


# ----------------- Endpoints -----------------

@app.get("/health")
def health_check():
    """Health check endpoint answering 200 when ready."""
    return {"status": "ok"}


@app.post("/messages", response_model=MessageResponse)
def handle_message(req: MessageRequest, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """
    Handles incoming rider message.
    Idempotent: If message_id was already processed, returns cached reply.
    """
    existing = db.query(ConversationMessage).filter(
        ConversationMessage.message_id == req.message_id

def call_groq_chat(
    messages: List[Dict[str, str]],
    temperature: float = 0.0,
    max_retries: int = 5
) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Calls Groq OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint.
    Handles HTTP 429 rate-limiting with exponential backoff and Retry-After header.
    """
    api_key = os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not api_key:
        return None

    model = os.getenv("GROQ_MODEL", "openai/gpt-oss-120b")
    url = "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": messages,
        "temperature": temperature
    }

    for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
        try:
            resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=25)
            if resp.status_code == 200:

1: """
2: Client for PaySwift Payouts API.
3: Handles:
4: - POST /v1/payouts with Idempotency-Key
5: - GET /v1/payouts?rider_id={rider_id}
6: - Retries with backoff on 429 (rate limit) or 5xx server errors
7: - Idempotency / 409 Conflict handling
8: """
9: 
10: import os
11: import time
12: import uuid
13: import logging
14: from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Any
15: import requests
16: 
17: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
18: 
19: class PaySwiftClient:
20:     def __init__(self, base_url: Optional[str] = None):
21:         raw_url = base_url or os.environ.get("PAYSWIFT_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8081")
22:         self.base_url = raw_url.rstrip("/")
23: 
24:     def get_rider_payouts(self, rider_id: str, max_retries: int = 3) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
25:         """
26:         Retrieves all payouts recorded in PaySwift for this rider.
27:         GET /v1/payouts?rider_id={rider_id}
28:         """
29:         url = f"{self.base_url}/v1/payouts"
30:         params = {"rider_id": rider_id}
31: 
32:         for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
33:             try:
34:                 resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5)
35:                 if resp.status_code == 200:
36:                     data = resp.json()
37:                     if isinstance(data, list):
38:                         return data
39:                     return data.get("data", data.get("payouts", []))
40:                 elif resp.status_code in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504):
41:                     logger.warning("PaySwift GET returned status %d. Retry %d/%d", resp.status_code, attempt, max_retries)
42:                     time.sleep(0.5 * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
43:                     continue
44:                 else:
45:                     logger.error("PaySwift GET error %d: %s", resp.status_code, resp.text)
46:                     return []
47:             except requests.RequestException as e:
48:                 logger.warning("PaySwift GET connection failed (%s). Retry %d/%d", str(e), attempt, max_retries)
49:                 time.sleep(0.5 * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
50:         return []

1: # Submission logistics
2: 
3: - `docker compose up` starts your whole system: your service, Postgres and the `payswift` service already defined in `docker-compose.yml`. Keep the `payswift` service as it is.
4: - Your service listens on port **8000** and answers `GET /health` with 200 when it is ready.
5: - Your service reads the PaySwift URL from the environment variable `PAYSWIFT_BASE_URL`.
6: - `POST /messages` returns `{"reply": "..."}`. You may add fields; we only rely on `reply`.
7: - `GET /trace/{rider_id}` returns a JSON list of steps in order. Each step has at least:
8:   `at` (ISO time), `type` (`message_in`, `tool_call`, `decision`, `reply`, or `error`), `name`, `input`, `output`.
9: - `GET /ops/pending` returns a JSON list of items waiting for ops. Each item has at least:
10:   `id`, `rider_id`, `type` (`approval` or `escalation`), `amount` (rupees, for approvals), `reason`, `created_at`.
11: - Your eval command is one line in your README and takes the service URL as its argument, for example `python evals/run.py http://localhost:8000`.
12: - List every environment variable your service needs in `.env.example`. Don't commit `.env` or any key.
13: - `ai-logs/` holds the raw exports of the AI sessions you used, one file per session. Where to find them:
14:   Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` · Codex CLI: `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-*.jsonl` or `codex export` ·
15:   Cursor: chat menu (…) → Export Chat · GitHub Copilot in VS Code: Command Palette → "Chat: Export Chat…" ·
16:   Gemini CLI: `/export jsonl --output <file>` · Antigravity: the chat export, or the `antigravity-history` tool · ChatGPT: Settings → Data controls → Export.
17:   If your tool has no export, include whatever it does provide and say what it is.
18: - We use whatever is on `main` of the repo you link when the deadline passes.
19: 
20: ## Output shapes
21: 
22: Only the shape is fixed. Step names, what goes in `input` and `output`, and how many steps there are depend entirely on how you design your agent.
23: 
24: `GET /trace/{rider_id}`
25: 
26: ```json
27: [
28:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "message_in", "name": "<name>", "input": {"message_id": "...", "text": "...", "received_at": "..."}, "output": null},
29:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "tool_call",  "name": "<your tool>", "input": {"<argument>": "..."}, "output": {"<result>": "..."}},
30:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "decision",   "name": "<what was decided>", "input": {"...": "..."}, "output": {"...": "..."}},
31:   {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "reply",      "name": "<name>", "input": null, "output": "<text sent to the rider>"}
32: ]
33: ```
34: 
35: `GET /ops/pending`
36: 
37: ```json
38: [
39:   {"id": "<id>", "rider_id": "<rider>", "type": "approval", "amount": 120, "reason": "<why it needs a human>", "created_at": "<ISO time>"},
40:   {"id": "<id>", "rider_id": "<rider>", "type": "escalation", "amount": null, "reason": "<why it needs a human>", "created_at": "<ISO time>"}
41: ]
42: ```
